Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute shortness of breath with pleuritic right-sided back pain when taking a deep breath; cough with blood on two occasions today.
  - Subjective fever. No clear trigger/exposure identified (no recent long-haul travel; no smoking).
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Dyspnea and pleuritic right back pain began today with two brief hemoptysis episodes.
  - Fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance for ~2 weeks prior.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat swelling/closure sensation: not documented.
  - Voice change/hoarseness: not documented.
  - Dysphagia/odynophagia: not documented.
  - Drooling: not documented.
  - Nasal/ocular symptoms: not documented.
  - Stridor/noisy breathing: not documented.
  - Dyspnea: present.
  - Swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): not documented.
  - Ear symptoms: not documented.
  - Neck pain/swelling: denies palpable neck lumps; self-palpation “normal.”
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - No prior similar episodes reported.
  - No history of venous thromboembolism (VTE); no family VTE history.
  - No recent long-haul flights.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: none known.
  - Medications: Methotrexate (indication: SLE); dose/route/frequency not documented; last taken this morning.
- Any relevant social context:
  - Non-smoker; works a desk job; lives alone in a flat; has a cat.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  - No facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling reported or observed.
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - Patient reports dyspnea. No stridor or noisy breathing reported.
- Mental status and associated features:
  - Alert and interactive on video; no dizziness/syncope reported.
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Pulse (self-counted radial): regular, approximately 66–74 bpm.
  - Capillary refill: normal on video demonstration.
  - Oropharynx: visualized; appeared normal.
  - Cervical lymph nodes: patient self-palpation—no enlargement felt.
  - Blood pressure, temperature (objective), respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, chest exam: Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient:
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression:
  - Suspected lower respiratory tract infection (community-acquired pneumonia with pleuritic pain) requiring in-person assessment.
- Evidence summary:
  - Acute onset of pleuritic right-sided back pain, dyspnea, subjective fever, and two brief hemoptysis episodes; immunosuppressed host (SLE on methotrexate). Appears stable remotely with normal pulse and capillary refill.
- Differential diagnosis (aligned with DDx):
  1) Community-acquired pneumonia with pleurisy (high): fever, pleuritic pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis; immunosuppression increases risk. Opposing: objective fever and focal lung findings not yet documented.
  2) Pulmonary embolism with pulmonary infarction (medium): pleuritic pain, dyspnea, hemoptysis; SLE increases thrombotic risk. Opposing: normal pulse, subjective fever, no travel/immobilization or VTE history.
  3) Acute bronchitis (medium): acute cough/fever with minor hemoptysis possible; opposing: localized pleuritic pain and immunosuppression favor pneumonia.
- Additional note:
  - Lung cancer concern discussed; presentation is atypical for malignancy (abrupt onset with fever/pleurisy in a nonsmoker). Consider chest imaging if symptoms persist or do not resolve.
- No transcript–DDx conflicts identified.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Same-day face-to-face clinic review arranged to:
    - Auscultate chest.
    - Check blood pressure, pulse, temperature, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate.
    - Decide on need for antibiotics and further testing.
  - No prescriptions issued pending in-person assessment.
  - Confirmed no antibiotic allergies.
- Specific instructions:
  - Call practice support team using number provided in the appointment notes to book the face-to-face slot today.
  - Rest and avoid exertion until reviewed.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Seek urgent care/EMS if any of the following occur before the appointment: worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, persistent or large-volume hemoptysis, fainting/dizziness, new confusion, high fever/rigors, or new leg swelling/pain.
- Follow-up:
  - Anticipate antibiotic therapy if pneumonia confirmed.
  - Consider chest X-ray (and further workup) if symptoms do not improve or if exam suggests alternative diagnoses (including PE evaluation if indicated).
  - Reassure regarding low immediate likelihood of lung cancer; re-evaluate if persistent hemoptysis or unresolved symptoms.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vitals: temperature, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation.
  - Chest auscultation and focused respiratory exam.
  - Hemoptysis characterization (volume, color, clots), sputum description, TB risk factors/travel/exposures.
  - Methotrexate dose/route/frequency; recent lab monitoring (CBC/LFTs) not documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; minor audio interruptions and a brief name discrepancy in the conversation.
